title: Shahid Kapoor, Rashmika Mandanna, and Kriti Sanon Just Launched Cocktail 2’s First Songs — and the NRI Love Triangle Reboot Is Looking Dangerously Fun
excerpt: The original Cocktail was a love letter to Indians in London. The sequel trades Deepika and Saif for a new trio, drops its trailer May 29, and hits theatres June 19.
body:
If you’re an NRI of a certain vintage, the original Cocktail (2012) wasn’t just a movie — it was a mirror. Saif Ali Khan, Deepika Padukone, and Diana Penty navigating love, identity, and that specific brand of South Asian chaos in London flats and Soho clubs? That was half the diaspora’s twenties condensed into two hours.

Fourteen years later, Maddock Films is taking another shot at the formula — and the early signs suggest they’re not playing it safe.

The New Trio

Cocktail 2 stars Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna in what’s being positioned as a “spiritual sequel” — new characters, new story, same emotional territory. Homi Adajania returns to direct, with Dinesh Vijan producing alongside Luv Ranjan.

At a song launch event at a Mumbai restobar on May 17, the three leads previewed two unreleased tracks: ‘Mashooka’ (featuring Shahid and Kriti) and ‘Tujhko’ (featuring Shahid and Rashmika). Music director Pritam Chakraborty was also in attendance — a signal that the soundtrack will be a major campaign pillar, just as it was for the original.

The event’s headline moment? Rashmika Mandanna praising Kriti Sanon and accidentally dropping an expletive on camera while calling her “hot.” She immediately backpedalled — “Censor kar dena! I didn’t say that!” — but the clip was already going viral. It’s exactly the kind of candid, unscripted energy that suggests genuine chemistry between the cast, not just marketing-deck harmony.

The Campaign Is Already Clever

Maddock’s promotional strategy is interesting. Instead of a standard single-song drop, they’re letting fans vote on which track releases first — turning the audience into participants rather than passive consumers. The winning song will be the first official release. In an era where Bollywood marketing often feels formulaic, giving fans a direct say is a sharp, youthful move that fits the brand.

Shahid Kapoor set the tone at the event: “I’m very fortunate to have worked with these two amazing actresses, superstars and beautiful ladies who are extremely professional and in the absolute prime of their careers. Both have given spectacular performances and look amazing. That’s why my character, Kunal, can’t decide who to go with. That’s what the film is all about.”

The trailer drops May 29. Theatrical release is locked for June 19, 2026.

Why the Diaspora Is Already Circling

The original Cocktail earned its cult status among NRIs for a simple reason: it took their world seriously. The London setting wasn’t exotic tourism — it was lived reality. The characters dealt with identity questions that felt specific to Indians abroad: who you become when you’re far from home, how love gets complicated when your cultural defaults clash with your actual desires.

Whether the sequel captures that same specificity remains to be seen. The cast upgrades are notable — Shahid Kapoor is a more dynamic leading man than Saif was in 2012, and having both Rashmika and Kriti means Maddock has two of Bollywood’s biggest current draws sharing the frame. The question is whether Homi Adajania and writers can find a fresh emotional frequency rather than simply recreating the original’s dynamics with newer faces.

Luv Ranjan, co-producing, seemed aware of the weight: “I’m scared because the first part was written by Imtiaz Ali. I told Dino and Homi, ‘Better make a good film.’ Or else, sabse zyada gaali mujhe padegi.”

What NRIs Should Know

  • Trailer: May 29, 2026
  • Release: June 19, 2026 (theatrical)
  • Director: Homi Adajania (Cocktail, Finding Fanny)
  • Music: Pritam (confirmed — songs ‘Mashooka’ and ‘Tujhko’ previewed)
  • Producers: Dinesh Vijan (Maddock Films) + Luv Ranjan

For NRIs who’ve been waiting for a Bollywood romance that speaks to their experience — not just at them — Cocktail 2 is the one to track. The original earned its place in the diaspora canon. The sequel has the cast, the director, and the pedigree. Now it just needs the story to match.
